cells.border_score.note: NotImplementedError: Physical boundaries are unknown: this environment's outline was inferred from positions, bins or a mask, not declared as a wall or drop edge, and it has no named walls. Declare what the outline is: Environment.from_polygon(outline, bin_size) for a walled arena, or arena=OpenArena(outline, outline='drop') for an elevated track or platform (MaskArena(..., outline=...) for a mask). Boundary-based rate maps also need bin support at the measured boundaries; attaching an arena does not extend bins or supply missing observations. Alternatively, explicitly choose boundary_source='analysis' to use retained bin edges as an approximation.

behavior.laps.note:
InputError: detect_laps(method='auto') counts laps around a loop, but this environment has no loop: its track graph has no cycle, or its area has no hole to run around.
Why: on a track, a tree maze or in an open arena the animal can always come back the way it went, so no lap goes round a loop and the laps found would have direction 'unknown'.
Fix: for back-and-forth runs on a linear track or arm, use detect_trials(env, times, positions, regions=[start, end]); to segment round trips against a template, pass method='reference' with reference_lap=, which reports each round trip's direction along the track as 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

hazards.message:
All 29 units are silent from 5865.3 s to 7081.0 s (1216 s) while position is tracked. If the electrophysiology was not recording then, pass spike_window=(start, stop) so that time is excluded from occupancy.
74813/74813 spike_times (100%) across all neurons fell outside the position time window [5865.15, 7081]; spike_times.min()=5.86519e+06 spike_times.max()=7.08097e+06. The spike times span 1.21578e+06 and reach 7.08097e+06, about 1000 times the 1215.84 s of times: if spike_times are in milliseconds, divide them by 1000. Check that spike_times and times share units (both seconds). Dropped spikes do not contribute. Set warn_on_drop=False to suppress this warning.

bin_size=2.5 is at least the per-axis data extent [0.9035, 0.8743] in every dimension.
Why: this produces very few bins, and it is often a units mistake: positions in m but bin_size meant in cm, for example.
Fix: check that bin_size and positions use the same units, then use a bin_size well below the data extent, such as bin_size=0.02
